Definition: from G1537 and G4492; to uproot:--pluck up by the root, root up.
BiblicalUsage: Scripture uses ekrizóō where we would say to uproot. In Matthew 13:29, the text says "ye root up also the wheat with them." In Matthew 15:13, the text says "shall be rooted up."
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that ekrizóō matters because God's judgment is just, and it falls where it should — no one escapes it, and no one suffers it unjustly. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
